title: Exenatide, a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, may negatively impact bone healing in rats: histopathological, biochemical, and in silico findings.
authors: Ugur, Fatih; Yilmaz, Ibrahim; Guner, Ersin; Albayrak, Mehmet; Taskin, Recep; Sarikas, Nurtac; Bildirici, Mehmet Akif; Dellalbasi, Ayse Basak; Ozcan, Candemir
journal: Journal of orthopaedic surgery and research
one_liner_zh: 该研究用分子对接评估Exenatide与GLP-1受体及成骨转录因子的结合，但核心是药物对骨愈合的动物实验，蛋白质-DNA互作非主要对象，方法仅简单对接，深度不足。
abstract: BACKGROUND: This study evaluates the effects of exenatide (EXE), a glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist, on bone healing in rats using a single radius cortical defect model and histopathological, biochemical, and in silico methods. METHODS: Forty-two male Sprague-Dawley rats, excluding controls, were divided into 7 groups after receiving a standard radius defect. The serum levels of total protein (TP), calcium (Ca(2+)), phosphorus (P), alkaline phosphatase (ALP), osteocalcin (OC), tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-alpha), and interleukin-6 (IL-6) in each specimen were measured. Radius samples were examined histopathologically using hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) and Masson's trichrome staining. Molecular docking analyses were used to assess EXE interactions with the GLP-1 receptor and osteogenic transcription factors. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. RESULTS: Changes in the selected serum markers were observed in the blood samples obtained from the specimens; however, these changes may not have been due to EXE administration. No significant negative effect on bone healing was observed in the groups that received subcutaneous EXE after the bone defect was created. By contrast, it was observed that for the treatment group that received EXE for 7 consecutive days before the bone defect was created on Day 7, bone healing progressed more slowly than in the groups treated with saline. Regarding the binding of EXE to the other target receptors, root mean square deviation (RMSD) values were low, bruised surface area (BSA) was high, and electrostatic interactions were strong, indicating that the ligand (i.e., EXE) binds to the selected receptor surfaces. CONCLUSION: Although the data obtained from the in vitro analyses in this study were verified using molecular docking, it should be noted that its design is preclinical. Given the widespread clinical use of GLP-1 receptor agonists in the management of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), our research findings may have translational relevance. Although derived from an experimental animal model, these results suggest that GLP-1 agonists such as EXE can exert additional effects on bone healing and inflammatory processes, thus warranting further studies, including controlled clinical investigations, to elucidate the potential implications for patient care.
abstract_zh: 背景：本研究通过单半径皮质缺损模型，结合组织病理学、生物化学及计算机模拟方法，评估艾塞那肽（EXE）——一种胰高血糖素样肽-1（GLP-1）受体激动剂——对大鼠骨愈合的影响。方法：将42只雄性Sprague-Dawley大鼠（对照组除外）在建立标准半径缺损后分为7组。测定每份标本血清中总蛋白（TP）、钙（Ca(2+)）、磷（P）、碱性磷酸酶（ALP）、骨钙素（OC）、肿瘤坏死因子-α（TNF-α）和白细胞介素-6（IL-6）的水平。使用苏木精和伊红（H&E）及Masson三色染色对半径样本进行组织病理学检查。采用分子对接分析评估EXE与GLP-1受体及成骨转录因子的相互作用。统计学显著性设定为p < 0.05。结果：在标本获取的血样中观察到所选血清标志物的变化；然而，这些变化可能并非由EXE给药所致。在骨缺损创建后接受皮下EXE注射的各组中，未观察到对骨愈合的显著负面影响。相反，在骨缺损创建前连续7天接受EXE治疗的第7天组中，观察到骨愈合进展比生理盐水处理组更慢。关于EXE与其他靶受体的结合，均方根偏差（RMSD）值较低，接触表面积（BSA）较高，静电相互作用较强，表明配体（即EXE）与所选受体表面结合。结论：尽管本研究中体外分析获得的数据已通过分子对接验证，但应注意其设计属于临床前阶段。鉴于GLP-1受体激动剂在2型糖尿病（T2DM）管理中广泛临床应用，我们的研究结果可能具有转化相关性。尽管这些结果源自实验动物模型，但提示EXE等GLP-1激动剂可能对骨愈合和炎症过程产生额外影响，因此有必要开展进一步研究，包括对照临床调查，以阐明对患者护理的潜在影响。
